title: How Long Does a Settlement Take in Washington?
metaDescription: How long car accident settlements take in Washington: District of Columbia timelines, medical liens, and negotiation phases.
excerpt: Educational Washington, DC guide — 3-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: District of Columbia deadline overview
paragraphs: Most District of Columbia car accident injury lawsuits must be filed within **3 years** of the injury date. Missing this deadline can permanently bar recovery.
Wrongful death, government-entity, and minor claimant cases may follow different rules. This article is educational — confirm your dates with a licensed District of Columbia attorney.

sections.heading: Why waiting hurts Washington claims
paragraphs: With ~1,082 annual crashes in the Washington area, evidence fades fast: skid marks wash away, witnesses relocate, and video is overwritten.
Insurers begin building a file immediately. Early recorded statements can lock in descriptions before you know the full extent of injuries.

sections.heading: Comparative fault in District of Columbia
paragraphs: District of Columbia follows Contributory negligence rules. If you are found partially at fault, compensation may be reduced or barred depending on your percentage.
Document everything that supports the other driver's negligence — traffic citations, 911 calls, and witness statements.

sections.heading: Insurance minimums and coverage gaps
paragraphs: District of Columbia requires at least 25/50/10 in liability coverage (verify current law). Many at-fault drivers carry only minimums.
Review your declarations page for UM/UIM, MedPay, and PIP. These coverages can matter when the other driver is uninsured or underinsured in Washington.

sections.heading: Government and special entities
paragraphs: Claims involving city buses, state vehicles, or federal property often require earlier notice than the standard 3-year window. Missing a notice deadline can defeat an otherwise valid claim.

sections.heading: Practical timeline for Washington residents
paragraphs: Day 1–7: Medical care, police report, insurer notification (facts only).
Week 2–8: Follow treatment plans, gather bills, avoid social media posts about the crash.
Month 2+: If injuries continue, consult counsel before accepting settlement releases.

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my Washington case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in District of Columbia?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 3-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
